questions.question: Q1. According to the Arrhenius relationship modeled in the simulation, how does elevating the temperature from 25°C to 55°C impact battery aging kinetics?

answers.a: It causes a linear reduction in capacity fade per cycle.
answers.b: It drives an exponential acceleration in the wear rate multiplier.
answers.c: It eliminates overpotentials by increasing electrolyte viscosity.
answers.d: It fixes the wear factor at a constant baseline value of 0.005%.

explanations.a: Temperature acceleration in degradation kinetics is non-linear.
explanations.b: Correct. Arrhenius rate equations state that reaction rates double exponentially with temperature rises.
explanations.c: Elevated temperatures decrease electrolyte viscosity rather than eliminating overpotentials.
explanations.d: The wear factor scales dynamically with temperature.

questions.question: Q2. If the battery capacity fade increases over a large number of cycles, what happens to the internal resistance (R_int) according to the scaling formula?

answers.a: It scales down inversely to match the lower available capacity.
answers.b: It scales up proportionally, increasing by 2% for every 1% of capacity fade.
answers.c: It remains entirely clamped at the baseline factory value of 10 mΩ.
answers.d: It drops to zero once the battery reaches the End-of-Life (EOL) threshold.

explanations.a: Internal resistance increases as capacity degrades.
explanations.b: Correct. SEI growth and electrode degradation simultaneously reduce capacity and elevate internal impedance.
explanations.c: Internal resistance escalates with degradation cycling.
explanations.d: Resistance reaches peak values at EOL rather than dropping to zero.

questions.question: Q3. During the simulation run, selecting the 'Extreme Track' driving pattern card (100% discharge load) causes which effect?

answers.a: A dramatic spike in volumetric heat flux (Q_flux) due to the squared load term.
answers.b: A complete cessation of internal Joule heating indicators.
answers.c: A slow, highly optimal depletion of the State of Charge (SoC).
answers.d: Automatic activation of the normal charging profile modifier.

explanations.a: Correct. Heat generation scales quadratically with current (I^2 * R), causing severe thermal flux under 100% load.
explanations.b: Joule heating increases significantly under high discharge loads.
explanations.c: High load causes rapid, non-optimal SoC depletion.
explanations.d: Discharging under extreme load does not activate charging profiles.

questions.question: Q4. What visual alert state occurs inside the volumetric 3D module grids when operating under severe thermal stress or high loads?

answers.a: The module boxes scale down and turn a bright cyan color.
answers.b: The cylinder matrices develop visible micro-crack overlays and shift colors from green toward deep red.
answers.c: The green status LED turns off completely and the coolant ports vanish.
answers.d: The busbars change into insulated plastic structures.

explanations.a: Severe stress triggers warm amber/red color transitions.
explanations.b: Correct. Thermal stress visualization renders red overlays and degradation indicators on module graphics.
explanations.c: Coolant indicators remain active during stress monitoring.
explanations.d: Busbar visual structures remain fixed metallic representations.

questions.question: Q5. What is the secondary consequence of internal resistance escalation as the cell continuously degrades?

answers.a: It generates higher internal heat generation, creating an aging acceleration loop.
answers.b: It protects active particle structures from volumetric micro-cracking.
answers.c: It forces the thermal runaway risk index to stay locked at 0%.
answers.d: It decreases the battery cell core temperature below ambient levels.

explanations.a: Correct. Higher resistance produces higher I^2*R heat, which further accelerates chemical degradation in a feedback loop.
explanations.b: Resistive heating accelerates mechanical stress and cracking.
explanations.c: Thermal runaway risk increases with resistance escalation.
explanations.d: Increased heat generation raises core temperature above ambient.
